raw_record.question_text: If $J,P,$ and $L$ are the midpoints of $\overline{KH}, \overline{HM}$ and $\overline{MK}$, respectively. Find $z$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as triangle KHM with J on KH, P on HM, and L on MK. The drawn cevians MJ, KP, and HL meet at Q. From the text, J, P, and L are midpoints, so these cevians are medians. Use the centroid theorem: the three medians meet at the centroid Q, which divides each median in a 2:1 ratio, with the longer part adjacent to the vertex. On median MJ, the image labels MQ = 4 and QJ = 2z. Therefore MQ:QJ = 2:1, so 4:(2z)=2:1. Hence 2z=2 and z=1.

method.method_draft: Read from the diagram that Q lies on segment MJ, with MQ labeled 4 and QJ labeled 2z. From the text, J is the midpoint of KH, while P and L are also midpoints, so Q is the common intersection of the three medians. Instead of simply quoting the centroid ratio, derive it with vectors: let the position vectors of K, H, and M be k, h, and m. Since J is the midpoint of KH, j=(k+h)/2. The centroid/intersection of medians has position q=(k+h+m)/3. Rewrite q in terms of j and m: q=(2j+m)/3, so Q is two-thirds of the way from M to J. Thus MQ = 2/3 MJ and QJ = 1/3 MJ, giving MQ:QJ=2:1. The image gives MQ=4 and QJ=2z, so 4/(2z)=2, implying z=1.
